question.prompt: Given point \(A(-2,3)\), point \(B\) is the reflection of \(A\) across the \(x\)-axis, and point \(C\) is the reflection of \(A\) across the \(y\)-axis. Find the area of \(\triangle ABC\).

solutions.explanation: \(B(-2,-3)\) and \(C(2,3)\). \(AB\) is perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis and has length 6; \(AC\) is parallel to the \(x\)-axis and has length 4. Since \(\angle A=90^\circ\), the area is \(6\times4\div2=12\).
solutions.title: Coordinate reflections and triangle area
